correctness.rationale: For all strictly interior parameters, deterministic annual bank memory gives B_(t+1)=Y_t, and independent seedling sources give q_yz=(1-d)[1-(1-c)(1-g0)^y(1-g1)^z]. The strict observable domain and four-parameter inverse follow by exact algebra, with determinant -(1-c)^2(1-d)^3 g0 g1. Stationary pair balance yields only two ratios from two years, giving two-dimensional fibers; three years reveal all four q_yz values. A standalone 256-tuple exact rational test and symbolic Jacobian have passed. The proof addresses all quantified claims; no finite experiment is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The main ecological source supplies the four-state model and interior identifiability, but its inspected main text does not give the exact 3-census minimal-horizon theorem, global observable inverse, or complete feasible transition-table inequalities. Follow-up three-year simulation pertains to scenario discrimination, not this exact four-parameter result. Related HMM and noisy-OR techniques are acknowledged prior art. Historical priority is provisional in view of inaccessible supplements and a possible broader identifiability theorem.

The result is structurally rather than empirically validated, and is specific to deterministic one-year seed-bank memory.

value.rationale: A natural finite monitoring-design question receives a sharp answer: three yearly population-law observations suffice and two do not. The exact feasible observable table supplies a falsifiability criterion for the original ecological model, and the rational inverse separates colonization, immediate germination, delayed germination and disturbance without extra hidden-state ambiguity. The exact theorem concerns ideal population probabilities rather than finite-patch estimation; ecological importance is motivated by the source papers on unobservable dormant stages.
